headlines.title: Kraken’s Krak Moves Into Credit With Two US Cards, One Backed by a USDC Deposit
headlines.summary: The Kraken parent’s money app is taking waitlist sign-ups for two Visa cards that pay up to 4% cashback in dollars or bitcoin, with a launch set for early 2027.

headlines.title: Visa (V) Broadens Checkout Options On Its Acceptance Platform
headlines.summary: Visa (NYSE: V) is expanding its partnership with Klarna to embed Klarna’s payment options into the Visa Acceptance Platform. Merchants in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and Europe gain access to pay-in-full, interest-free instalments, and longer-term financing at checkout. The Klarna integration is designed to simplify technical setup for merchants by routing multiple payment options through Visa’s existing acceptance infrastructure.

description: Visa Inc. operates as a payments technology company in the United States and internationally. It operates VisaNet, a transaction processing network that enables authorization, clearing, and settlement of payment transactions. The company also offers credit, debit, and prepaid card products; tap to pay, tokenization, and click to pay services; Visa Direct, a platform which facilitates money movement, enabling clients to collect, hold, convert, and send funds across its network; and issuing solutions, such as airport lounge access, dining reservations, shopping experiences, event tickets, and seller offers. In addition, it provides acceptance solutions, an omnichannel payment integration with e-commerce platforms; risk detection and prevention solutions; and advisory and other services comprising consulting practice, proprietary analytics models, data scientists and economists, marketing services, and managed services. The company provides its services under the Visa, Visa Electron, V PAY, Interlink, and PLUS brands. It serves consumers, sellers, financial institutions, and government entities. Visa Inc. was founded in 1958 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
